source: An uncharged capacitor acts like a wire; a full one passes no current.
Students think current flows through a fully charged capacitor.

A capacitor in a circuit behaves in two simple ways at the two ends of time, which is all most exam questions need. The in-between is the RC circuit curve. Each problem here is one short scene and a chain of questions. Answer them in order: each later question uses what you found before, so a slip early on carries through. Keep full precision between steps and round only at the end.

Just after switching on, an uncharged capacitor has no voltage: treat it as a wire. Long after, a full capacitor passes no current: treat it as a break. Then $$Q = CV_C, \qquad U = \tfrac{1}{2}CV_C^2,$$ with $V_C$ the voltage of whatever sits beside it.
At first the moving charges go into the capacitor; as it fills, they switch over to R₂.

A $12\ \text{V}$ battery, a switch and $R_1 = 20\ \Omega$ are in series with $R_2 = 40\ \Omega$ and an uncharged $50\ \mu\text{F}$ capacitor in parallel. Find (1) the current at the start, (2) the current long after, (3) the capacitor's charge.
(2) No current into the full capacitor: $I = 12/60 = 0.2\ \text{A}$.

Thinking current flows steadily through a capacitor. Charge piles up on its plates, but none crosses the gap; once full, its branch carries nothing. Check: in steady state, the circuit without the capacitor branch must give the same currents.
